questions.prompt: Which statement best describes Social Studies as a learning area?
options: It studies people, places, resources, culture and governance
It studies only calculations with numbers
It studies only drawing and painting
questions.correctAnswer: It studies people, places, resources, culture and governance
questions.explanation: Social Studies brings together knowledge about people, their environment, economic activities, culture and systems of governance.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the scope and importance of Social Studies in personal and community life.

questions.prompt: Which career is most directly linked to map reading and interpretation skills?
questions.correctAnswer: Cartographer
questions.explanation: A cartographer prepares and interprets maps, so map reading is a key skill in that career.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify career pathways that use knowledge and skills from Social Studies.

questions.prompt: Which action best addresses gender stereotypes in choosing Social Studies careers?
options: Encouraging learners of all genders to explore any suitable career
Telling girls to avoid leadership careers
Telling boys to avoid caring careers
Choosing careers only because friends chose them
questions.correctAnswer: Encouraging learners of all genders to explore any suitable career
questions.explanation: A learner's interests, ability and values should guide career choice, not gender stereotypes.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how to challenge gender stereotypes in career and entrepreneurial choices.

questions.prompt: Why is an integrated approach useful when learning Social Studies?
options: It connects geography, history, economics and citizenship in real situations
It removes the need to study society
It limits learners to one type of source
It makes all topics about weather only
questions.correctAnswer: It connects geography, history, economics and citizenship in real situations
questions.explanation: Social issues often involve places, people, resources, culture and governance at the same time.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the value of learning Social Studies through connected ideas and situations.

questions.prompt: A class wants to promote social cohesion during group work. Which value should they practise most?
questions.correctAnswer: Respect
questions.explanation: Respect helps learners listen to one another and work together despite differences.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify values promoted through learning Social Studies.

questions.prompt: Which map element tells the reader what a map is about?
questions.correctAnswer: Title
questions.explanation: The title names the place or theme shown on a map.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common map elements and explain their uses.

questions.prompt: On a map, 1 cm represents 5 km on the ground. What ground distance is represented by 4 cm?
questions.correctAnswer: 20 km
questions.explanation: Multiply 4 by 5 km because each centimetre on the map represents 5 km on the ground.
questions.learningOutcome: Use a simple map scale to calculate real ground distance.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of a key or legend on a map?
options: To explain symbols used on the map
To show the map author's age
questions.correctAnswer: To explain symbols used on the map
questions.explanation: A key or legend helps the reader understand what map symbols and colours mean.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret conventional symbols used on maps.

questions.prompt: What do contour lines that are very close together usually show on a topographical map?
questions.correctAnswer: A steep slope
questions.explanation: Close contour lines show that height changes quickly over a short distance, which means the slope is steep.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret simple topographical map features using contour patterns.

questions.prompt: Which line of latitude passes through Kenya?
questions.correctAnswer: Equator
questions.explanation: The Equator crosses Kenya and helps describe Kenya's position on the globe.
questions.learningOutcome: Use latitude and longitude to describe the location of places in Africa.

questions.prompt: Lines of longitude are most useful when learners want to compare what between places?
questions.correctAnswer: Time
questions.explanation: Longitudes are used to calculate local time because the earth rotates through 15 degrees in about one hour.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate lines of longitude to time differences between places.

questions.prompt: Town A is at 30 degrees East and Town B is at 45 degrees East. If Town A is at noon, what is the time at Town B?
questions.explanation: Town B is 15 degrees east of Town A, so it is one hour ahead.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate simple time differences using longitudes.

questions.prompt: Which physical feature runs through parts of Kenya, Tanzania and Ethiopia?
questions.correctAnswer: The Great Rift Valley
questions.explanation: The Great Rift Valley is a major landform that stretches through several countries in Eastern Africa.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify major physical features found in Kenya and Eastern Africa.

questions.prompt: Why are highland areas such as around Mount Kenya generally cooler than lowland areas?
options: Highlands are always closer to deserts
questions.correctAnswer: Temperature decreases as altitude increases
questions.explanation: Altitude affects climate; higher places usually have lower temperatures than nearby lowlands.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how altitude influences temperature and human activities.

questions.prompt: Which human activity is commonly supported by lakes such as Lake Victoria?
questions.correctAnswer: Fishing
questions.explanation: Large lakes support fishing, transport, tourism and water supply in nearby communities.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate physical features to human activities in Kenya and Eastern Africa.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly links the Indian Ocean to economic activity along Kenya's coast?
options: It supports fishing, port trade and beach tourism
It prevents all forms of transport
It removes the need for conservation
questions.correctAnswer: It supports fishing, port trade and beach tourism
questions.explanation: The coast benefits from ocean resources, ports, marine transport and tourism, but these resources still need protection.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how water bodies influence settlement and economic activities.

questions.prompt: Which weather element is measured using a thermometer?
questions.correctAnswer: Temperature
questions.explanation: A thermometer measures how hot or cold the air is.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify weather instruments and the elements they measure.

questions.prompt: A class wants to know the direction from which wind is blowing. Which instrument should they use?
questions.correctAnswer: Wind vane
questions.explanation: A wind vane shows wind direction, while other instruments measure different weather elements.
questions.learningOutcome: Select suitable weather instruments for school weather observation.

questions.prompt: Which action would make a school rain gauge reading more reliable?
options: Place it in an open area away from roofs and trees
Place it directly under a classroom roof
Keep it indoors near a window
questions.correctAnswer: Place it in an open area away from roofs and trees
questions.explanation: A rain gauge should collect rainfall directly without extra water from roofs or blockage from trees.
questions.learningOutcome: Use weather instruments correctly to collect and interpret weather data.

questions.prompt: Which factor explains why coastal areas often have a smaller temperature range than inland dry areas?
questions.correctAnswer: Distance from the sea
questions.explanation: Large water bodies heat and cool slowly, so they moderate temperatures in nearby coastal areas.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain factors that influence climate in Kenya and Eastern Africa.

questions.prompt: Which climatic region in Eastern Africa is most associated with very low rainfall and sparse vegetation?
questions.correctAnswer: Desert and semi-desert
questions.explanation: Desert and semi-desert areas receive little rainfall, so vegetation is usually sparse and drought-resistant.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify main climatic regions and their characteristics in Eastern Africa.

questions.prompt: Which vegetation type is most likely to support large numbers of grazing wild animals in Eastern Africa?
questions.correctAnswer: Savanna grassland
questions.explanation: Savanna grasslands provide pasture for many herbivores, which also supports wildlife tourism.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate vegetation zones to wildlife and human activities.

questions.prompt: Which conservation practice can help restore degraded vegetation in a school compound?
options: Burning all grass after every lesson
questions.correctAnswer: Planting and caring for trees
questions.explanation: Tree planting, watering and protecting seedlings help restore vegetation and reduce soil erosion.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply simple practices for conserving vegetation in the locality.

questions.prompt: Which historic built environment is found in Mombasa and is linked to Indian Ocean trade history?
questions.correctAnswer: Fort Jesus
questions.explanation: Fort Jesus is a historic built site in Mombasa that reflects the coast's long trading and colonial history.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify historic built environments in Kenya and Eastern Africa.

questions.prompt: Why should learners help conserve historic built environments such as Gedi ruins and Lamu Old Town?
options: They preserve heritage and support learning and tourism
They are useful only as playgrounds
questions.correctAnswer: They preserve heritage and support learning and tourism
questions.explanation: Historic built environments keep evidence of the past and can also support education, identity and responsible tourism.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of conserving historic built environments.

questions.prompt: Which strategy best protects a historic site from damage by visitors?
options: Use guided paths, signs and community education
Allow visitors to remove stones as souvenirs
Build houses inside the protected ruins
Let livestock graze through fragile walls
questions.correctAnswer: Use guided paths, signs and community education
questions.explanation: Guided access and community education reduce damage while allowing people to learn from the site.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse suitable ways of conserving historic built environments in the locality.

questions.prompt: Why is Africa often described as the cradle of humankind?
options: Many early human fossils have been found in Africa
All modern cities began in Africa
All continents were once part of Kenya
questions.correctAnswer: Many early human fossils have been found in Africa
questions.explanation: Fossil discoveries from places such as Eastern Africa provide evidence of early human origins.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain evidence used to show Africa as an early centre of human origins.

questions.prompt: Which site in northern Kenya is well known for fossil evidence of early human life?
questions.correctAnswer: Koobi Fora
questions.explanation: Koobi Fora near Lake Turkana is known for important fossil finds linked to early human history.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify key archaeological sites linked to early human history in Eastern Africa.

questions.prompt: Which source would provide the strongest evidence when studying early human remains?
questions.correctAnswer: Archaeological fossils and tools
questions.explanation: Fossils and tools are primary evidence that can be examined to understand early human life.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish reliable sources of evidence for studying early human history.

questions.prompt: Why did Ancient Egypt grow strongly along the River Nile?
options: The river provided water, fertile silt and transport
The river froze all year for roads
The river made rainfall unnecessary everywhere in Africa
questions.correctAnswer: The river provided water, fertile silt and transport
questions.explanation: The Nile supported farming, settlement and movement, which helped Ancient Egyptian civilisation grow.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain factors that contributed to the growth of early African civilisations.

questions.prompt: Which contribution is associated with Ancient Egypt?
questions.correctAnswer: Hieroglyphic writing and pyramid building
questions.explanation: Ancient Egypt is known for developments such as hieroglyphic writing, architecture and organised government.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify achievements of selected early African civilisations.

questions.prompt: Which pair contains examples of Bantu-speaking communities in Kenya?
questions.correctAnswer: Kikuyu and Luhya
questions.explanation: Kikuyu and Luhya are examples of Bantu-speaking communities in Kenya.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify selected communities in Eastern Africa according to language groups.

questions.prompt: Which pair contains examples of Cushitic-speaking communities in Eastern Africa?
questions.correctAnswer: Somali and Borana
questions.explanation: Somali and Borana are commonly classified among Cushitic-speaking communities in Eastern Africa.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify selected communities in Eastern Africa according to language groups.

questions.prompt: Which factor could have pushed communities to migrate from an area in the past?
questions.correctAnswer: Drought and shortage of pasture
questions.explanation: Drought and shortage of pasture could force communities to move in search of food, water and grazing land.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain reasons for migration and settlement of selected communities.

questions.prompt: Which outcome can result when different communities migrate and settle near one another?
options: Exchange of ideas, trade and intermarriage
questions.correctAnswer: Exchange of ideas, trade and intermarriage
questions.explanation: Migration can lead to cultural exchange, trade, intermarriage and sometimes conflict over resources.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse effects of migration and settlement on communities in Eastern Africa.

questions.prompt: What does population density mean?
options: The number of people living in a unit area
The number of rivers in a county
The total length of roads in a country
The amount of rainfall in a season
questions.correctAnswer: The number of people living in a unit area
questions.explanation: Population density compares the number of people with the size of the area they occupy.
questions.learningOutcome: Define population density and use it to describe settlement patterns.

questions.prompt: Why are fertile highland areas in Kenya often more densely populated than arid areas?
options: They support farming, water supply and cooler living conditions
They have no roads or markets
They are always covered by desert sand
questions.correctAnswer: They support farming, water supply and cooler living conditions
questions.explanation: Fertile soils, reliable rainfall, water and favourable temperatures attract settlement and farming.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain physical and human factors influencing population distribution.

questions.prompt: Which problem is most likely in a very densely populated rural area with limited farmland?
options: Land subdivision into very small plots
questions.correctAnswer: Land subdivision into very small plots
questions.explanation: High population pressure can lead to land fragmentation, pressure on services and competition for resources.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse effects of high and low population density on communities.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes an age set in many African traditional societies?
options: A group of people initiated or recognised within a similar age group
questions.correctAnswer: A group of people initiated or recognised within a similar age group
questions.explanation: Age sets helped organise duties, identity and social responsibilities in some communities.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the role of age groups and age sets in African traditional societies.

questions.prompt: Which was a common function of a clan in African traditional society?
options: Providing identity, support and marriage rules
questions.correctAnswer: Providing identity, support and marriage rules
questions.explanation: Clans helped people know their relatives, responsibilities, support networks and marriage restrictions.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain functions of clans and other social units in traditional society.

questions.prompt: Which example is an aspect of culture?
questions.correctAnswer: Language
questions.explanation: Culture includes language, beliefs, food, dress, music, values and ways of life.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify aspects of culture in communities.

questions.prompt: Which cultural practice should be preserved because it promotes positive values?
options: Storytelling that teaches honesty and responsibility
questions.correctAnswer: Storytelling that teaches honesty and responsibility
questions.explanation: Positive cultural practices that teach values and identity should be preserved, while harmful practices should be rejected.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate cultural practices that promote values and social wellbeing.

questions.prompt: Which method can help preserve a community's oral traditions for future learners?
questions.correctAnswer: Recording elders' stories with permission
questions.explanation: Recording and sharing oral traditions respectfully can preserve knowledge while recognising the community source.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply respectful ways of preserving cultural heritage.

questions.prompt: Which classroom behaviour promotes inclusion among learners from different communities?
options: Refusing to work with new learners
questions.correctAnswer: Listening respectfully to different viewpoints
questions.explanation: Inclusion grows when learners respect identity, listen fairly and avoid stereotypes.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate ways of promoting inclusion and respect for diversity.

questions.prompt: Which factor most likely caused pastoral communities to move in search of new grazing areas?
questions.correctAnswer: Shortage of pasture and water
questions.explanation: Pastoral migration was often influenced by the need for pasture and water for livestock.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate migration patterns to environmental and economic needs.

questions.prompt: Which approach is best when learners compare different origin stories from communities?
options: Respect the stories and compare them with historical evidence
Assume every story is a modern law
questions.correctAnswer: Respect the stories and compare them with historical evidence
questions.explanation: Origin stories are important cultural sources, and historical inquiry also checks evidence such as archaeology and linguistics.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse oral traditions respectfully alongside other historical sources.

questions.prompt: A settlement grows around a busy market and road junction. Which factor best explains this growth?
options: Trade and transport links attract people
questions.correctAnswer: Trade and transport links attract people
questions.explanation: Transport and trade create jobs, services and movement, which can attract settlement.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how transport and economic activities influence settlement patterns.

questions.prompt: Which action would help reduce conflict between farmers and pastoralists during a dry season?
options: Agreeing on shared water points and grazing routes
questions.correctAnswer: Agreeing on shared water points and grazing routes
questions.explanation: Dialogue and agreed resource-sharing rules can reduce conflict over scarce water and pasture.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse ways communities can manage shared resources peacefully.

questions.prompt: Which example best shows interdependence among people in a community?
options: Farmers sell food to traders who supply households
A market closes to prevent exchange
questions.correctAnswer: Farmers sell food to traders who supply households
questions.explanation: Interdependence means people rely on one another for goods, services, ideas and support.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe ways people depend on one another in communities.

questions.prompt: A learner is preparing a report on population distribution. Which data would be most useful?
options: The number of pencils in a desk
questions.correctAnswer: Population figures and area size
questions.explanation: Population distribution and density need information about people, area and settlement patterns.
questions.learningOutcome: Select relevant data for describing population distribution.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes a resource?
options: Something useful that people can use to meet needs
Any object that has no value
A rule that stops all work
questions.correctAnswer: Something useful that people can use to meet needs
questions.explanation: Resources may be natural, human or made by people, and they help satisfy needs or support production.
questions.learningOutcome: Define resources and identify examples found in Eastern Africa.

questions.prompt: Which factor favours beef farming in many pastoral areas of Eastern Africa?
questions.correctAnswer: Availability of grazing land
questions.explanation: Beef farming needs pasture, water, suitable breeds and markets for animals and animal products.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain factors influencing beef farming in Eastern Africa.

questions.prompt: Which challenge commonly affects pastoral beef farming during prolonged drought?
options: Too much fish in the ocean
questions.correctAnswer: Shortage of pasture and water
questions.explanation: Drought reduces pasture and water, weakening livestock and lowering production.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify challenges facing beef farming and suggest practical responses.

questions.prompt: Which practice would make fishing in Lake Victoria more sustainable?
options: Using recommended net sizes and observing closed seasons
questions.correctAnswer: Using recommended net sizes and observing closed seasons
questions.explanation: Sustainable fishing protects young fish and breeding areas so fish stocks can recover.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate responsible fishing practices in Eastern Africa.

questions.prompt: Which fishing method is commonly used by small-scale fishers in lakes and coastal waters?
questions.correctAnswer: Net fishing
questions.explanation: Nets are commonly used in fishing, though fishers must use the correct mesh size to protect young fish.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common fishing methods used in Eastern Africa.

questions.prompt: Which factor promotes wildlife tourism in Eastern Africa?
options: Rich wildlife in national parks and reserves
questions.correctAnswer: Rich wildlife in national parks and reserves
questions.explanation: Wildlife, scenery, culture, security, transport and hospitality services help attract tourists.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain factors promoting tourism in Eastern Africa.

questions.prompt: Which action best supports sustainable tourism at a national park?
options: Following park rules and avoiding littering
questions.correctAnswer: Following park rules and avoiding littering
questions.explanation: Responsible visitors protect wildlife habitats and help tourism continue without damaging the environment.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply responsible practices that conserve tourism resources.

questions.prompt: Which mode of transport is usually most flexible for door-to-door movement of goods?
questions.correctAnswer: Road transport
questions.explanation: Road transport can reach many homes, farms, markets and schools directly.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare modes of transport and their uses in Eastern Africa.

questions.prompt: Why is railway transport useful for carrying bulky goods over long distances?
options: It can carry large loads at a relatively lower cost
It can fly over every mountain
It needs no stations or tracks
It is only used for sending text messages
questions.correctAnswer: It can carry large loads at a relatively lower cost
questions.explanation: Railways are useful for heavy or bulky goods such as minerals, fuel and agricultural produce over long distances.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain advantages of different transport modes for trade and production.

questions.prompt: Which challenge commonly affects road transport in some rural areas during heavy rains?
options: Roads may become muddy, slippery or impassable
questions.correctAnswer: Roads may become muddy, slippery or impassable
questions.explanation: Poor road surfaces and drainage can make movement difficult during heavy rainfall.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify challenges facing transport networks in Eastern Africa.

questions.prompt: Which example shows how mobile communication can support farmers?
options: Farmers receive market prices before selling produce
Mobile phones replace all soil nutrients
questions.correctAnswer: Farmers receive market prices before selling produce
questions.explanation: Communication networks help people share prices, weather alerts, payment information and market opportunities.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how communication supports trade and community development.

questions.prompt: Which mineral is mined at Lake Magadi in Kenya?
questions.correctAnswer: Soda ash
questions.explanation: Lake Magadi is known for soda ash, which is used in industries such as glass manufacture.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify selected minerals and mining areas in Eastern Africa.

questions.prompt: Which measure reduces environmental damage from mining?
options: Restoring mined land and controlling waste
questions.correctAnswer: Restoring mined land and controlling waste
questions.explanation: Responsible mining should reduce pollution, protect people and rehabilitate land after extraction.
questions.learningOutcome: Suggest ways of reducing negative effects of mining on people and the environment.

questions.prompt: What is trade?
options: The buying and selling or exchange of goods and services
questions.correctAnswer: The buying and selling or exchange of goods and services
questions.explanation: Trade allows people and countries to exchange what they produce for what they need.
questions.learningOutcome: Define trade and identify forms of trade in Eastern Africa.

questions.prompt: Which example describes an export from Kenya?
options: Tea sold from Kenya to another country
A phone bought from another country for use in Kenya
Rainfall measured in a school compound
A road built between two classrooms
questions.correctAnswer: Tea sold from Kenya to another country
questions.explanation: An export is a good or service sold to another country, while an import is bought from another country.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish between imports and exports using local examples.

questions.prompt: What happens when a country imports much more than it exports over a long period?
options: It may face an unfavourable balance of trade
It becomes unable to produce anything
questions.correctAnswer: It may face an unfavourable balance of trade
questions.explanation: Buying more from other countries than it sells can create pressure on foreign exchange and trade balances.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse simple effects of imports and exports on a country's economy.

questions.prompt: Which value addition activity could increase income from fish?
options: Cleaning, cooling, smoking or packaging fish before sale
Throwing fish back after they spoil
questions.correctAnswer: Cleaning, cooling, smoking or packaging fish before sale
questions.explanation: Value addition improves quality, shelf life and market value of products.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how value addition can improve income from economic activities.

questions.prompt: Which school enterprise project uses local resources responsibly?
options: Growing vegetables using compost and harvested water
Cutting all school trees for charcoal
questions.correctAnswer: Growing vegetables using compost and harvested water
questions.explanation: A good enterprise project meets needs, uses resources responsibly and observes health and environmental care.
questions.learningOutcome: Design simple enterprise ideas that use local resources sustainably.

questions.prompt: Which farming activity is common in Kenya's cool and wet highland areas?
questions.correctAnswer: Tea growing
questions.explanation: Tea grows well in cool, wet highland areas with suitable soils.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate climate and relief to selected agricultural activities.

questions.prompt: Which practice helps farmers produce crops in dry areas where rainfall is unreliable?
questions.correctAnswer: Irrigation
questions.explanation: Irrigation supplies water to crops when rainfall is low or unreliable.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify farming practices that support production in dry areas.

questions.prompt: Which leader is remembered for resisting colonial rule among the Giriama at the coast?
questions.correctAnswer: Mekatilili wa Menza
questions.explanation: Mekatilili wa Menza is remembered as a Giriama leader who mobilised resistance against colonial rule.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify selected traditional leaders and their contributions in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Kivoi wa Mwenda is commonly associated with which activity in Kenyan history?
questions.correctAnswer: Long-distance trade and Akamba leadership
questions.explanation: Kivoi wa Mwenda is remembered in relation to Akamba leadership and long-distance trade networks.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe contributions of selected traditional leaders in Kenya.

questions.prompt: What was one role of councils of elders in many traditional Kenyan communities?
options: Settling disputes and guiding community decisions
questions.correctAnswer: Settling disputes and guiding community decisions
questions.explanation: Councils of elders helped resolve conflicts, advise communities and maintain order.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain roles of traditional governance institutions.

questions.prompt: The Njuri Ncheke is best described as which type of institution?
options: A council of elders among the Ameru
A modern county assembly in Mombasa
questions.correctAnswer: A council of elders among the Ameru
questions.explanation: The Njuri Ncheke is a traditional council of elders associated with the Ameru community.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify examples of traditional governance systems in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which action shows responsible citizenship at school?
options: Following agreed rules and respecting others' rights
questions.correctAnswer: Following agreed rules and respecting others' rights
questions.explanation: Responsible citizens respect rules, protect property, help others and uphold rights and duties.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify qualities and actions of a responsible citizen.

questions.prompt: Which is one way a person may become a Kenyan citizen?
options: By birth or registration as provided by law
By visiting Kenya for one day
By naming a social media account Kenya
questions.correctAnswer: By birth or registration as provided by law
questions.explanation: Kenyan citizenship is acquired through legal ways such as birth or registration under the Constitution and citizenship laws.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe lawful ways of acquiring citizenship in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Why is the Constitution of Kenya important?
options: It is the supreme law that guides government and protects rights
It is only a list of market prices
It is used only for weather forecasting
questions.correctAnswer: It is the supreme law that guides government and protects rights
questions.explanation: The Constitution sets out rights, values, government structures and principles for public life.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of the Constitution of Kenya for social wellbeing.

questions.prompt: Which pair contains national values listed in Article 10 of the Constitution of Kenya?
questions.correctAnswer: Patriotism and national unity
questions.explanation: Article 10 includes values such as patriotism, national unity, human dignity, equity, social justice, integrity and accountability.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify national values and explain their role in good governance.

questions.prompt: Which action helps protect the Constitution of Kenya in everyday life?
options: Respecting rights and following lawful procedures
questions.correctAnswer: Respecting rights and following lawful procedures
questions.explanation: Citizens protect the Constitution by respecting rights, obeying lawful processes and holding leaders accountable.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse ways citizens can uphold and protect the Constitution of Kenya.

questions.prompt: What is democracy?
options: A system where people participate in choosing leaders and making decisions
A system where no citizen has a voice
questions.correctAnswer: A system where people participate in choosing leaders and making decisions
questions.explanation: Democracy values participation, representation, accountability and respect for the will of the people.
questions.learningOutcome: Define democracy and identify democratic practices.

questions.prompt: Which situation best shows representative democracy?
options: Citizens elect leaders to make decisions on their behalf
Only one person makes all decisions without consultation
Learners are forbidden to vote for class leaders
questions.correctAnswer: Citizens elect leaders to make decisions on their behalf
questions.explanation: In representative democracy, people choose representatives to make decisions for the community or country.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish between direct and representative democracy.

questions.prompt: Why is public participation important in governance?
options: It allows citizens to share views before decisions are made
It prevents citizens from asking questions
questions.correctAnswer: It allows citizens to share views before decisions are made
questions.explanation: Public participation improves decisions because leaders hear community needs, ideas and concerns.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of public participation in democratic governance.

questions.prompt: What does the rule of law mean?
options: Everyone, including leaders, should follow the law
questions.correctAnswer: Everyone, including leaders, should follow the law
questions.explanation: The rule of law means laws apply fairly to all people and public authority must be exercised lawfully.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the meaning and importance of the rule of law.

questions.prompt: Which branch of government interprets laws and settles legal disputes?
questions.correctAnswer: Judiciary
questions.explanation: The judiciary interprets laws and resolves disputes through courts and related institutions.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the main arms of government and their roles.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains why separation of powers is important?
options: It checks misuse of power by sharing roles among government arms
It gives all power to one office
It removes the need for courts
questions.correctAnswer: It checks misuse of power by sharing roles among government arms
questions.explanation: Separation of powers helps the executive, legislature and judiciary check one another and protect constitutional governance.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse why separation of powers supports accountable governance.

questions.prompt: Which service is commonly associated with county governments in Kenya?
questions.correctAnswer: County health services
questions.explanation: County governments handle devolved services such as county health, local roads, markets and some agricultural services.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify selected functions of county governments in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which method is a peaceful way of resolving conflict between two school clubs?
options: Mediation by a trusted neutral person
questions.correctAnswer: Mediation by a trusted neutral person
questions.explanation: Mediation helps parties discuss the issue with a neutral person and look for an acceptable solution.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify peaceful methods of resolving conflicts in society.

questions.prompt: A conflict has started because two groups need the same watering point. Which first step is most constructive?
options: Bring representatives together for dialogue on sharing rules
Encourage each group to attack first
Hide all information from the community
Block elders and local leaders from helping
questions.correctAnswer: Bring representatives together for dialogue on sharing rules
questions.explanation: Dialogue allows groups to explain needs and agree on fair rules before conflict worsens.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply peaceful conflict resolution methods to resource-sharing situations.

questions.prompt: Which is an example of government revenue?
options: Taxes collected from citizens and businesses
Rain falling on a school farm
A mountain range on a map
questions.correctAnswer: Taxes collected from citizens and businesses
questions.explanation: Government revenue includes taxes, fees, grants and other funds used to provide public services.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify sources of government revenue.

questions.prompt: Which example shows government expenditure for public welfare?
options: Keeping all taxes in private homes
questions.correctAnswer: Building hospitals and maintaining roads
questions.explanation: Government spends revenue on public needs such as health, education, roads, security and administration.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain ways national and county governments spend public revenue.

questions.prompt: Which action best shows accountability in using public funds?
options: Publishing clear reports on how money was spent
questions.correctAnswer: Publishing clear reports on how money was spent
questions.explanation: Accountability requires openness, records, audits and honest reporting on the use of public resources.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse practices that promote accountability and transparency in governance.

questions.prompt: Which climate change adaptation strategy is suitable for a dry farming area?
options: Harvesting rainwater and planting drought-tolerant crops
questions.correctAnswer: Harvesting rainwater and planting drought-tolerant crops
questions.explanation: Water harvesting and drought-tolerant crops help communities cope with unreliable rainfall.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate sustainable lifestyle practices for adapting to climate change.

questions.prompt: A school wants to reduce erosion on a bare slope. Which plan is most effective?
options: Plant grass and trees while controlling runoff
Dig channels straight down the slope
questions.correctAnswer: Plant grass and trees while controlling runoff
questions.explanation: Vegetation cover and runoff control slow moving water and protect soil from erosion.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse conservation actions that protect physical features and soil.

questions.prompt: Which conclusion is best if a place has reliable rainfall, fertile soils, good roads and many job opportunities?
options: It is likely to attract a higher population density
It will always become a desert
questions.correctAnswer: It is likely to attract a higher population density
questions.explanation: Favourable physical conditions and economic opportunities often attract people and services.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse combined factors that influence population distribution.

questions.prompt: A class is creating a simple class constitution. Which first step is most democratic?
options: Discuss shared values and agree on rules through participation
Let one learner secretly write all rules
Copy rules that punish only one group
questions.correctAnswer: Discuss shared values and agree on rules through participation
questions.explanation: A democratic constitution-making process includes participation, shared values, rights, duties and fair procedures.
questions.learningOutcome: Create simple governance rules that reflect constitutional values and participation.

questions.prompt: Which tourism plan best balances income and conservation in a wildlife area?
options: Limit visitor damage, employ local guides and fund habitat protection
Build hotels on animal breeding grounds
Allow unlimited littering for more visitors
questions.correctAnswer: Limit visitor damage, employ local guides and fund habitat protection
questions.explanation: Sustainable tourism should protect wildlife, support local livelihoods and maintain resources for the future.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate tourism strategies that balance economic benefits and conservation.

questions.prompt: Which proposal best uses communication technology to improve trade among small traders?
options: Create a shared phone group for prices, orders and delivery updates
Ban traders from sharing market information
Hide all prices until goods spoil
questions.correctAnswer: Create a shared phone group for prices, orders and delivery updates
questions.explanation: Timely communication helps traders compare prices, coordinate transport and reduce losses.
questions.learningOutcome: Create practical ways communication can improve trade and livelihoods.

questions.prompt: Which question best helps evaluate whether a school enterprise project is sustainable?
options: Does it earn income while protecting health, people and the environment?
Does it use resources carelessly for quick money?
Can it ignore hygiene and still sell food?
Can it avoid keeping any records?
questions.correctAnswer: Does it earn income while protecting health, people and the environment?
questions.explanation: A sustainable enterprise considers profit, safety, fairness, resource use and environmental care.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate enterprise ideas for sustainability and community benefit.

questions.prompt: Which action best promotes national unity during a school cultural day?
options: Celebrate different cultures respectfully and include all learners
Rank cultures as superior and inferior
questions.correctAnswer: Celebrate different cultures respectfully and include all learners
questions.explanation: Respectful cultural exchange strengthens unity, dignity and appreciation of diversity.
questions.learningOutcome: Create inclusive activities that promote national unity and respect for diversity.

questions.prompt: Which plan best combines Social Studies knowledge to solve a local littering problem?
options: Map affected areas, involve residents, set rules and organise clean-up teams
Ignore the problem until drains block
questions.correctAnswer: Map affected areas, involve residents, set rules and organise clean-up teams
questions.explanation: An integrated Social Studies response uses mapping, participation, responsibility, rules and community action.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a simple community action plan using Social Studies knowledge and values.

questions.explanation: From SOCIAL-STUDIES marking scheme.
